decisions.reason: The distributed ALCMS control unit sits in the firm's core airfield lighting business, has long installed-base lifecycles and costs little to keep offered, so the option stays open while airport demand recovers after the pandemic.
The air situation display complements the surveillance portfolio around the flagship MLAT system, and its value remains uncertain but cheap to preserve given slow tower-system procurement cycles.
A training program is a low-cost service offering tied to the installed base, so keeping it open has little cost even though uptake is uncertain.
The airfield ground lighting course supports the firm's core lighting customers at minimal carrying cost, so there is no clear negative signal to justify abandoning it.

The collaboration software fits the strategic move toward collaborative decision-making, but its value is still unresolved after the pandemic shock, so the firm keeps it as an option while watching for possible consolidation into a broader platform.
As the flagship surveillance product with a strategic role and long ATC procurement cycles, the MLAT system warrants continued commitment rather than abandonment.
